problem_text:
A logistics center must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical fuel additive over a 16-week operational window.  
The starting stock at the commencement of the planning interval is 69 barrels.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 16 \), the distributor permits the center to submit a procurement request, the volume of which must fall between 3 and 52 barrels.  
Nevertheless, every request issued will undergo a 2‑week transit delay before it becomes available to meet consumption or replenish reserves.  
The consumption of the additive each week is specified as follows:  
* Week 1: 52 barrels  
* Week 2: 46 barrels  
* Week 3: 39 barrels  
* Week 4: 26 barrels  
* Week 5: 44 barrels  
* Week 6: 20 barrels  
* Week 7: 38 barrels  
* Week 8: 35 barrels  
* Week 9: 10 barrels  
* Week 10: 16 barrels  
* Week 11: 10 barrels  
* Week 12: 16 barrels  
* Week 13: 31 barrels  
* Week 14: 56 barrels  
* Week 15: 23 barrels  
* Week 16: 29 barrels  

Supply deficits are tolerated; however, any unsatisfied consumption is entirely forfeited and not carried forward.  
Throughout the planning window, additive quantities may be treated as continuous, and the aggregate volume of physical stock on hand at any moment must not surpass the storage‑tank capacity of 69 barrels.  

In week 2, the maximum procurement volume allowed is 18 barrels.  
In week 4, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 21 barrels.  

The aggregate expense over the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement expense, amounting to 1 per barrel ordered; the storage expense, amounting to 1 per barrel retained from one week to the next; and the deficit penalty, amounting to 14 per barrel of unmet consumption.  
Ascertain the optimal procurement volume for each week and monitor the consequent stock and deficit levels so as to minimize the total expense.
